units.source_text: “既然没能使自己沉溺于书堆中，有一段时间，我又试图让心灵浸泡在酒精里，以求忘却自我。

en.t: Since I had been unable to lose myself among piles of books, for a time I tried instead to soak my heart in alcohol, hoping to forget myself.

units.source_text: 我本不爱喝酒，却是天生能喝酒，因此我就想借酒量来灌醉自己的灵魂。

en.t: I did not particularly like drinking, but I was naturally able to hold my liquor, so I tried to use that capacity to intoxicate my own soul.

units.source_text: 这种浅薄的权宜之法，没过多久就使我变得更加厌世了。

en.t: This shallow makeshift remedy soon made me even more weary of the world.

units.source_text: 当我喝得烂醉的时候，会突然意识到自己的处境。

en.t: When I was dead drunk, I would suddenly become aware of my own situation.

units.source_text: 自己这般借酒浇愁，无异于自我欺瞒的蠢货。

en.t: I would realize that trying to drown my sorrow in drink like this made me nothing but a fool deceiving myself.

units.source_text: 于是，我战栗了，眼睛和心灵也随之清醒了。

en.t: Then I would shudder, and my eyes and heart would clear at once.

units.source_text: 有时候无论怎么喝，都装不出佯狂之态来，只是一味地消沉下去。

en.t: Sometimes, no matter how much I drank, I could not even pretend to be wildly drunk, and only sank deeper into gloom.

units.source_text: 即便用这些手段换来一时的愉快，而后必然会陷入更严重的忧郁之中。

en.t: Even if I gained a moment of pleasure by such means, afterward I was certain to fall into a still deeper melancholy.

units.source_text: 因为在自己最心爱的妻和她母亲面前，我必须时刻这样表现，而她们则是从女人的角度来解释我的所作所为。

en.t: For before the wife I loved most and her mother, I had to keep showing myself in that way, while they interpreted everything I did from a woman's point of view.
